cache.name: cache
cache.basis: `evict n spacing` over a spacing sweep. N_evict(spacing) is fitted against an exact enumeration of which walk addresses land in the target's set, which yields the ways and the conflict period (sets x line) with no special case for sub-line, line-sized or aliasing spacings. The line used is the measured fetch granularity; where the period is larger, the split between sets and line is reported as undetermined rather than assumed

tags vs bytes: with a 32 B fetch and a 65536 B conflict period the two models predict the same number (1), so the test cannot discriminate and no claim is made

8 configuration(s) hold nothing above the latch at all (waitstates=5 icache=0 dcache=0 wrhighfreq=0, waitstates=5 icache=0 dcache=0 wrhighfreq=1, waitstates=5 icache=0 dcache=0 wrhighfreq=2 ...): there the cache is switched off, which is a knob working rather than a geometry disagreeing

capacity floor: the target is first lost at a working-set span of 32768 B (spacing 512 B, n = 64) and is never lost below that in 417 further rows, the largest of which spans 32736 B. For a uniform walk the loss span is `ways x sets x line` for every spacing that divides the conflict period, so that smallest loss span IS the capacity, whatever the (ways, sets) split
caveats: 120 `evict` row(s) in this capture had their DISCARDED warm-up repetition disagree with the kept ones, in both directions (e.g. warm-up outlier: evict(192, 256) on flash first=18 median-of-rest=11). The discarded value is not in `obs[].raw`, so the kept repeats read `min == max` for rows the instrument itself reported as unstable. Every eviction-derived number here is a median of a filtered sample, and `min == max` on these rows is not evidence of reproducibility.

The eviction surface in waitstates=5 icache=0 dcache=1 wrhighfreq=0 is NOT a step function, so no (ways, sets, line) geometry is reported from it. At spacing 512 B the target is lost at n = 64 and present again at n = 65; 3 of 12 spacings behave that way. A threshold model is what `N_evict` means, and this configuration's own data falsifies it, so the ways, the sets and the conflict period are `unknown` rather than a fit to a model that does not hold. The CAPACITY survives, because it is read off the smallest loss span rather than fitted: that uses only the bottom edge of the surface, below every non-monotone row.

Two things look like this and they are not the same finding: a NON-DETERMINISTIC victim choice (the target survives past capacity some of the time), or an address-dependent effect the (ways, sets, line) family cannot express (the outcome depends on WHICH lines the walk ends on, not how many). They are separable by repeatability, and this capture cannot settle it: its own warnings record the DISCARDED warm-up repetition disagreeing with the kept ones on `evict` rows, so `min == max` over the stored repeats is a statement about a filtered sample. The replay control -- the same row re-measured later and in the opposite order -- is what settles it, not more repeats of one row.

The capacity is measured (32768 B) and the (ways, sets) split is NOT: 1-way x 1024 sets, 2-way x 512 sets, 4-way x 256 sets, 8-way x 128 sets, 16-way x 64 sets, 32-way x 32 sets, 64-way x 16 sets all predict the same loss span at every spacing this capture used, because a uniform walk at or below the conflict period loses the target after exactly `ways x sets x line` bytes however the two factors divide it. Separating them needs a spacing ABOVE the largest candidate period (32768 B), where the loss lands at n = ways directly: `evict n 65536` with n reaching 64, i.e. a probe region of at least 4259840 B -- or 589824 B to separate only the associativities an L1 plausibly has (<= 8-way, an architectural prior, stated here rather than applied silently). This shim's `evict` reaches 51200 B. The published geometry of this part is in the family; the tool does not pick from it.

replacement_policy.name: replacement_policy
evidence: the eviction surface is not monotone in the working-set size in the configuration with the most reuse, and every repeat of those rows carries no repeat information
caveats: LRU and FIFO are NOT separable with `memmap/1`'s two-argument primitives, and that is a property of the primitives rather than of the part. `walk` and `evict` produce a monotone reference string and `chase` a cyclic one, and on a cyclic string over capacity+1 lines LRU and FIFO evict exactly the same line at every step. Separating them needs a reference string that re-touches an already-resident line before bringing in a new one -- which is what the optional third `evict` argument provides, and what a shim that does not implement it leaves unreachable.

The cache claim reports no geometry here, so nothing below is sized from a measured associativity -- the probes are sized from a provisional fit and fire only if it happens to be close. Read a negative result as 'the instrument did not run', not as a property of the part. And the repeats cannot settle what the non-monotonicity means: this capture's own warnings record the DISCARDED warm-up repetition disagreeing with the kept ones on several `evict` rows, so `min == max` over the kept sample is not evidence that the measurement is reproducible. What settles it is the replay control -- the same row re-measured later and in the opposite order -- not more repeats of one row.
No eviction series in a set-associative configuration had both a determined transition and a spacing that is a multiple of the measured conflict period, so the step-sharpness instrument did not run.

The cyclic-chase discriminator did not run: it needs `chase` at two ADJACENT working-set sizes with a stride that is a multiple of the measured conflict period, in an isolated configuration. A chase whose stride is smaller than the conflict period never produces a conflict however large the working set, so it cannot reach the knee; and it needs a third, much larger working set to calibrate what a full thrash costs.

The re-touch probe (`evict n spacing -k*spacing`) contributed no usable row: either the shim does not honour the optional walk start, or no row was taken at a spacing that is a multiple of the measured conflict period with k below the measured associativity. Without it LRU and FIFO are not separable and neither is claimed.
The instruments did not agree, or none of them ran, so the policy is reported as unresolved rather than rounded to the nearer answer.

waitstate_scaling.basis: linear fit of the per-access cost against the `waitstates` knob, in each configuration separately; the headline coefficient is the latch differential in configuration 'dcache=0 icache=0 wrhighfreq=0'

caveats: A wait-state setting of 0 contributes a legitimate zero to this fit and must not be read as an absent structure: at LATENCY = 0 a hit and a miss cost the same cycle, so the structure is still there and simply worth nothing (MEASURING_CHANNELS B3).
At least one configuration shows a flat-zero differential at every wait state. That is the masking configuration (a cache holding both probe addresses), not evidence against the scaling.

twin_calibration.name: twin_calibration
twin_calibration.basis: the cold walk's `flash - twin` per-access cost measured at `waitstates = 0`, where a flash access is known to cost no more than an SRAM one, so anything left over is the harness. Computed per configuration and per loop body and never pooled across either; the headline is the isolated configuration, which is the one the structural claims are measured in
evidence: waitstates=0 icache=0 dcache=0 wrhighfreq=0: `reread` body over 6 point(s) -> flash-twin = +3.000 cyc/access
waitstates=0 icache=0 dcache=0 wrhighfreq=0: `walk` body over 2 point(s) -> flash-twin = +4.000 cyc/access
waitstates=0 icache=1 dcache=1 wrhighfreq=3: `reread` body over 6 point(s) -> flash-twin = +1.000 cyc/access
waitstates=0 icache=1 dcache=1 wrhighfreq=3: `walk` body over 2 point(s) -> flash-twin = +4.000 cyc/access
caveats: The twin is NOT a zero here: at `waitstates = 0`, where a flash access cannot cost more than an SRAM one, `flash - twin` still reads +4.000 cycles per access in waitstates=0 icache=0 dcache=0 wrhighfreq=0. A POSITIVE value means the flash path costs more than the dtcm twin even where the flash is free of wait states -- a fixed access cost that is not a flash structure. It is what a tightly-coupled twin looks like: a DTCM or similar zero-wait memory is not on the same fabric as the flash, so the subtraction leaves a constant behind rather than cancelling. It is large enough to matter: on this part it swallowed a one- and two-cycle latch differential whole, until the classification was moved inside the flash column. Every figure derived by subtracting the twin in this configuration carries that bias, and correcting means subtracting it. The instrument-neutral quantity is `flash(LATENCY) - flash(0)` at the same stride, which cancels the loop entirely.

The single-`reread` body reads +3.000 cycles in the same configuration, against +4.000 for the `walk` body. One number per (configuration, loop body) is the smallest honest unit: a longer loop body has idle cycles for an extra bus beat to hide in, so the two bodies are not interchangeable and are not averaged into one figure.
